Listeners will experience the thrill of exploration, the tension of survival, and the allure of the unknown, all while pondering the moral dilemmas presented by Nemo’s radical worldview. description:
Emma is a high achieving, middle class girl from west London. She seems destined for a successful career in banking and a comfortable British life. Until she makes a decision that will come to define her. In 2001 Emma marries Bashar al-Assad - the now infamous dictator of Syria.


In the early days, people inside and out of Syria dared to hope. Alongside his beautiful, progressive wife, Bashar promised to modernise the country.


But when the Arab Spring reached Syria in 2011, Bashar's regime showed itself for what it really was: a brutal force, willing to capture and kill ordinary Syrians demanding change. And in all the years that a war raged on, Asma stands by her husband. She seemingly ignored the desperate pleas to stop her husband from killing his own people. 


But what did she really know about the atrocities her husband’s government was carrying out? And what choices did she really have? Some people allege that she actually assisted the regime and cashed in on the war, that she herself is a war criminal. Others say she tried to run away but was trapped, held hostage by a regime who threatened her life and her children. 


So, who is the real Emma?

description:
Liftoff Journeys isn’t about polished success stories. It’s about the moments before success makes sense.

It was inspired by my three-year-old who told me, “I want to be a bubble bather when I grow up."   I realized that what she saw was that a bubble bath created joy, helped people, and made others feel good.Her instinct to do this in every roles she has had never disappeared.

This moment revealed something powerful to me: it’s the moments before success that shape who we become.Hosted by Jeanniey Walden, Liftoff Journeys features honest conversations with leaders, founders, and executives about how they actually built their lives and careers, through real decisions, detours, doubts, and defining moments.No bios. No highlight reels. Just authentic choices, inspired action, and relatable human experience.

At its core, the show reflects the mission of Liftoff Enterprises: helping leaders grow with confidence, clarity, and trust - in themselves and with others. These conversations echo the ideas behind my book The Trust Threshold: the point where self-doubt turns into momentum and leadership shifts from performance to presence.

There’s no single path to growth, but there are patterns.If you’ve ever wondered what happens before it all clicks, this podcast is for you.This is Liftoff Journeys.

title: New Teacher, Big Impact
author: Daryl Williams Jr
description:
Introducing the "New Teacher, Big Impact" podcast, where we equip new teachers with the tools to become more effective while prioritizing their well-being.

Have you ever felt burnt out, unsupported, or like you had to change who you are to make an impact in the classroom? Daryl knows exactly how that feels, and wants you to know that you don't have to struggle with those feelings. Join Daryl and other special guest educators as we explore the transformative power of discovering your "Teacher ID" – a journey that took him from being a terrible teacher to becoming a two-time Teacher of the Year.

In each episode, we'll dive deep into the core principles of teaching excellence:

Identify Your Dream: Reignite your passion for teaching by casting a vision that aligns with your purpose.

Illuminate Your Differences: Embrace your uniqueness and learn how to leverage it to make a profound impact on your students.

Ignore Your Doubters: Overcome self-limiting beliefs and fortify your mindset against external hurdles.

Improve Your Data: Master the Six Pillars of Effective Instruction:
1. Encourage: Create a classroom culture that supports student growth.

2. Engage: Manage the classroom, and craft lessons that capture attention.

3. Empower: Deliver content in a way that leads to information retention.

4. Evaluate: Utilize data to make informed decisions about instruction.

5. Extend: Continue growing in your learning and professional development.

6. Endure: Prioritize your well-being so that you can keep showing up.

Join us on the "New Teacher, Big Impact" podcast and learn how to be the teacher you've always wanted to be while making a lasting impact on your students' lives.

Vou explicar como Nuna afetou os níveis de oxigênio, os vulcões, os primeiros micróbios e por que a vida complexa talvez não existisse sem ele. Também comparamos Nuna com supercontinentes posteriores para mostrar como a Terra continua recombinando as mesmas peças com resultados completamente diferentes. É um lembrete de que a vida na Terra não apenas se adaptou à mudança — ela foi moldada pela colisão de continentes em escala planetária 🌍🧬

title: Things we pretend to understand
author: Raeesa
description:
Things We All Pretend to Understand

There are so many things in life that we pretend to understand just because everyone else seems to understand them. We nod when someone explains something complicated, laugh at jokes we did not get, and say “yeah, exactly” even when our minds are completely blank.

We pretend to understand adulthood, even though most of us are just figuring things out as we go. We pretend to know what we are doing with our careers, relationships, money, and future. We pretend to understand why people behave the way they do, why some friendships fade, and why certain things happen at the worst possible time.

Sometimes we even pretend to understand ourselves. We say we are fine when we are not, act like we know what we want, and convince ourselves that everything will eventually make sense.

Maybe the truth is that nobody understands everything. We are all learning, guessing, adapting, and pretending a little along the way. And perhaps admitting “I don't understand” is not a sign of weakness. It is simply being honest.

title: Porch Light: Conversations with Amikaeyla

description:
How are you, really?

Not the reflex answer. The one that lives in your body before it finds words — the one that arrives with a sigh, or a laugh, or a long pause while you both just breathe.

Every other week Amikaeyla pulls up a chair with someone whose life has taught them something true, and asks. She is a singer and sound practitioner, the originator of the Heart Voice Method, and she has sung her way across five continents. She knows what a single tone can do to a heart that has been running too long.

The porch is real. The wood creaks just right, the light is soft enough that you can actually see each other, and nobody is rushing anywhere.

You know that feeling when you are carrying something heavy, and you did not realize how heavy until someone asked if you wanted to set it down a minute? That.

These conversations go where they need to. From the last breath to the first sip of morning coffee. From what you have been holding in your shoulders since you were small to what your ancestors are still saying. From "am I doing this right?" to "who told you there was a right way?"

Dying, and how remembering it wakes you all the way up to living. Grief that never got its own room. Rest that does not have to earn its place. Rage that lights a room instead of burning it down. Forgiveness, the messy kind, the kind that changes you from the inside.

And always a good drink, a song that lands somewhere deep in your chest, and the kind of silence that feels like company.

Her guests are drummers and teachers, mystics and makers, people who walked through the fire and know something they cannot un-know.

No fixing. No performing. Just two people talking long enough for what is true to feel safe enough to show up.

New conversations every other week.

The light's on. Your chair is waiting. There's a drink poured. Come sit.

title: The Language Worker
author: Rita Prazeres Gonçalves
description:
Elevate your language business journey with The Language Worker, an audio podcast hosted by Rita Prazeres Gonçalves – founder of The Language Worker, terminology expert, business consultant and veteran podcaster with over 25 years in the language services industry. From big tech and LSPs to boutique agencies and solo businesses, Rita brings together everything she has learned as a Language Lead, Terminologist, Talent & Resource Management Consultant, trainer and host to help you build a sustainable, human‑centred language career.

In each episode, you will hear in‑depth, down‑to‑earth conversations about the real backstage of translation and localization: terminology and glossary work, translation project management, vendor and talent management, AI and MT workflows, SEO translation, and multilingual content that actually supports business goals. Rita talks with translators, project managers, vendor managers, founders, technology specialists and other language workers who share their experience, mistakes and practical strategies for navigating an ever‑changing industry. Topics include pricing and negotiation, client relationships, specialisation, leadership, ethical and sustainable language businesses, and how to design language work that fits your life instead of the other way around.

The Language Worker focuses on three main pillars – Talent, Training and Terminology – and how they show up in real language operations. You will find solo episodes that unpack corporate terminology and terminology governance in simple, practical terms, along with interviews that show why glossaries, termbases and style guides are the backbone of consistent, scalable multilingual content. Other episodes explore talent pathways and careers in the Language Industry, from freelancers and in‑house linguists to PMs, vendor managers and business owners, with plenty of mentoring‑style advice on CPD, networking and building confidence.

Whether you are a freelance translator, interpreter, subtitler, reviser, localization PM, vendor manager, language‑tech founder or head of an LSP, this podcast gives you actionable guidance on finding and keeping better clients, collaborating with LSPs and global teams, setting up workflows that scale, and using technology (including AI, CAT tools and TMSs) without losing the human side of language work. You will also hear about business growth, marketing and visibility for language professionals: niching, B2B case studies, thought leadership, podcasting, and turning your expertise into services that stand out

The Language Worker is the result of Rita’s deep gratitude for a life spent working with language – in tech companies, large and boutique LSPs, universities and now as a business owner. Think of it as a mix of practical business school, mentorship session and honest coffee chat in audio form, made for people who love languages and want their work to be meaningful, profitable and future-proof.

If you are searching in your podcast app for “translation business podcast”, “localization careers”, “terminology expert”, “how to start a language business”, “freelance translator tips”, “LSP growth strategy”, “vendor management in translation”, “AI and translation” or “ethical language services”, you are in the right place. Follow The Language Worker for regular episodes packed with insights, stories and concrete strategies to help linguists, localization professionals and language entrepreneurs create lasting impact and real business growth.

description:
Are you unsure of how and where to start when it comes to writing your book? Do you wish you knew how to organize and outline all your thoughts? Are you constantly doubting if you’re even qualified to write a story? Are you fearful of judgment from those closest to you?
I’m so glad you’re here! This podcast will help you learn step-by-step strategies on the writing process, teach you about the various publishing and marketing methods, and help you overcome self-doubt so you can build your confidence and finally take your book all the way from start to finish.
Hi, I’m Michelle, and I am a Christian, a mom, a wife, and - of course - a writer. For nearly 20 years I honed my craft in private, only ever writing behind a pen name. Although I was an accomplished and celebrated author in my online circle, I wouldn’t dare discuss my stories in person. I was ashamed and I knew I was being convicted by God to stop hiding behind a nickname and write something meaningful.
Motherhood, marriage, entrepreneurship, and busyness slowly started taking over my time. I didn’t know what to write anymore and I didn’t think I’d ever feel the satisfaction of finishing another story again, but God’s plan is far better than my own. 
Through prayer, dedication, and realistic time management, I am writing again with a renewed passion for telling stories that evoke emotion and I can’t wait to help you do the same! There is freedom and excitement in writing, sharing your stories, and connecting with others. If I can be bold and courageous with my words and learn how to stand in the strength of the Lord and put myself and my stories out there, then so can you. 
If you’re ready to finally find a way to make your writing process flourish and become a published author all while being a busy wife, mom, and churchgoer, follow along for 
- step-by-step processes that are simple and actionable 
- coaching that is encouraging and practical, and 
- results that can only come from faith and time with God. 
Pull out your laptop, grab a tasty drink and a treat and put those fingers to the keys: it’s time to start writing.

title: Living Grief: Honoring Loss Across Communities and Cultures
author: In Progress
description:
Living Grief: Honoring Loss Across Communities and Cultures is a community storytelling project that explores the many ways people experience, understand, and carry grief. 

Through a series of video stories, individuals reflect on loss in its many forms—from the death of loved ones to the loss of homeland, identity, relationships, culture, security, and belonging. Drawing on personal experience as well as cultural, spiritual, and generational traditions, Living Grief creates space for stories that are often difficult to name or share. Together, these reflections offer a living archive of how people remember, heal, adapt, and carry loss forward.

Living Grief is funded in part by the Minnesota Humanities Center with money from the Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund that was created with the vote of the people of Minnesota on November 4, 2008.

title: Immersive Japanese
author: Immersive Languages
description:
From Kav, creator of Immersive Languages and the hit Immersive Spanish podcast, comes Immersive Japanese, a different way to start speaking Japanese.


If you've tried learning Japanese before and felt overwhelmed, or been put off by the idea of spending months memorising alphabets and grammar before having a real conversation, this podcast is for you.

Immersive Japanese focuses on practical, real-world Japanese you can actually use. From ordering food and checking into a hotel to navigating Tokyo, visiting a convenience store and meeting new people, you'll learn the words and phrases you'd need on a real trip to Japan.


You'll be speaking Japanese from day one with our immersive speaking-gap method, giving you time to respond out loud and take part in the conversation yourself.

Each episode combines storytelling, immersive sound design and practical Japanese, placing you inside real situations as if you're actually travelling through Japan.


No endless vocabulary lists. No months of preparation before you speak.

Put your headphones on. Your trip to Japan starts here.

The Health Sciences Centre Foundation is shining a light on the lines that connect people to each other. The lines that connect generosity to investment; and that connect investment to better health care outcomes. The lines that connect discoveries to progress. And the lines that connect us all as a passionate community of Manitobans committed to excellence in health care today and for all time.
At the heart of every story and at the centre of every conversation is a simple idea: we can draw a solid line from the support of our community to meaningful change in people’s lives.
A new episode of Solid Lines is published every month.

title: EUREKA
author: Sami Gayle
description:
Eureka tells the true stories behind the inventions that built the modern world. Each episode, host Nirob takes one breakthrough — the printing press, penicillin, the light bulb, the telephone, the transistor, the vaccine, the internet — and traces its whole arc: the world before it existed, the restless mind that imagined it, the long and often bitter struggle to make it real, and the way it rippled outward to change how billions of people live.

These are not dry stories of gadgets. They are stories of people — dreamers and rivals, geniuses and frauds, the credited and the overlooked — and of the strange, winding, accidental paths that ideas take on their way to changing history. From the number zero to the machines that think, Eureka finds the human drama inside the history of ingenuity. Curious but accurate. Warm but honest. Clean and suitable for all ages. A new spark every week

Here are noble hearts tested by cruel society, faithful animals more virtuous than men, glittering salons shadowed by corruption, and lovers driven to sacrifice, rebellion, and despair.

These are tales of splendour and sorrow, of innocence in conflict with the world, read unabridged for those who still believe that literature should possess colour, feeling, and fire.

title: The Portrait of a Lady: A Journey of Choice and Consequence
author: Henry James
description:
Isabel Archer's desire for freedom takes a dark turn when she inherits a fortune that places her at the mercy of cunning manipulators. In Henry James's 'The Portrait of a Lady,' we dive into the tumultuous journey of a spirited American woman navigating the complex web of European society. As Isabel struggles against societal expectations and her own ambitions, she becomes ensnared in the schemes of those closest to her, including the enigmatic Gilbert Osmond, whose charm hides a chilling agenda.

This audiobook unpacks the central conflict between personal liberty and the constraints of wealth and influence. Listeners will experience Isabel's evolution from an idealistic young woman to someone grappling with the heavy consequences of her choices. Themes of betrayal, identity, and the pursuit of happiness resonate throughout, inviting deep reflection on what it means to truly live for oneself.

Join Isabel as she confronts the complexities of love, loyalty, and the price of freedom. Will her quest for autonomy result in liberation or entrapment? Discover the intricacies of her relationships and the haunting questions that arise as she seeks her own portrait of a life well-lived. Prepare for a captivating exploration of ambition and moral ambiguity that will leave you pondering long after the last chapter.

title: The Wind in the Willows: Adventures of Four Friends
author: Kenneth Grahame
description:
When the impulsive Toad of Toad Hall gets his hands on a flashy new motorcar, chaos ensues, leading him on a reckless adventure that threatens the peace of the entire riverbank community. In this enchanting audiobook, Kenneth Grahame weaves a tale of friendship, folly, and redemption through the lives of four beloved characters: the level-headed Rat, the wise and gentle Mole, the eccentric Toad, and the steadfast Badger. As Toad's obsession spirals out of control, his friends rally to save him from himself and reclaim Toad Hall from the villainous weasels who have taken over.

Explore themes of loyalty, the quest for identity, and the struggle between nature and modernity as you follow the ups and downs of this charming cast. Each character offers a unique perspective, bringing humor and heart to their journey along the riverbank. With rich descriptions and a mix of adventure and moral lessons, this classic tale invites listeners of all ages to reflect on their own friendships and the importance of community.

Join Toad, Rat, Mole, and Badger as they navigate the twists and turns of life, reminding us that true friendship can weather any storm. Dive into this timeless story, where every episode promises laughter, lessons, and a touch of magic in the everyday world.

description: Ever since I could remember there was music in my life or rattling around in my head. As I was born in 1966 I was too young to really appreciate the great musical styles of the times, but I was brought up on the 70’s music of 10cc, Bowie, Roxy Music etc. so all was not lost. I have been passionate about early Garage/Psych since my teenage years but I discovered very quickly that the more I was to delve into the past musically the more pathways and other avenues of musical styles opened up to me leading into a fascinating world of Blues, R ’n’ B, Rock, Soul,  Ska, Folk, Pop etc. After many happy years of collecting vast quantities of music from the era 1960 to about 1978, I started to wonder if there was anyone else out there in the big wide world who shared the same passion as I did. This in turn led me to seek out possible venues playing the kind of music I adored. But despite living just outside of Birmingham there was nothing happening locally. I found myself travelling to London to get my ‘fix’. As this was a logistical nightmare I started to look into a possible cheaper radio ‘fix’... surely there must be something happening? Actually I found much to my disappointment, very little or many dead links of now defunct shows. Well I decided I then only had one choice, to put on the sort of radio show that I would love to tune into myself and hopefully so would others. Well here we are with the finished product. The Good Man’s Radio Show. I hope you find yourself awfully glad that you stopped by my little bubble of joy and I am able to spread at least a little of the joy I feel myself when I listen to my music. If I can spread the word of all these (sometimes) forgotten gems and start a whole new generation of people looking to explore the possibility that music doesn’t have to be dull and lazy, which I tend to feel an awful lot is now sadly, then so much the better. Thanks for tuning in folks, enjoy the trip. .LemmyX

As a nurse, I spent years catching what others missed in patients. Then long COVID left me with racing heart rates, falls, and fatigue no one could explain — and I became the patient no one believed. It took 18 months of pushing for answers to get diagnosed with dysautonomia. The diagnosis brought grief for the body I used to trust, but also clarity. If your body says something's wrong and the tests say "normal," don't stop pushing. Be your own advocate — no one knows you like you do.

title: Nashvillains

description:
Nashvillains digs into the darkest true crimes in Music City's history. Serial killers who stalked its streets. A bomber who tried to bring it to its knees. Con artists, killers, and the occasional scandal from behind the studio glass.

Some of these cases made national headlines. Others were buried and nearly forgotten. All of them happened here, in the shadow of the honky-tonks.

Every episode is a  deep dive into a real case — the people, the motives, the moment everything turned. No dry true-crime checklist. Just gripping, edge-of-your-seat storytelling that gives these stories the weight they deserve.

A city this rich in music and heritage has more than a few dark tales woven into its history — and those stories deserve to be told.  Hit follow, and you'll never look at Music City the same way again.  Nashvillains.  Because sometimes it all comes down to three chords and a murder.

title: The Agrarian Librarian
author: Edmund Farms
description:
The Agrarian Librarian is a podcast about reevaluating our priorities, reducing unnecessary dependence, and becoming more connected to the people, places, and systems that sustain our lives.

Through conversations about philosophy, production, community, and politics, the show explores what happens when we redirect our attention away from distant institutions and abstract national debates and toward the people, places, skills, and systems directly around us.

Agrarianism here is not nostalgia or a rejection of technology and modern life. It is about recovering what remains valuable from the past while making thoughtful use of the present. It means understanding where things come from, developing useful skills, strengthening local relationships, producing more of what we need, and becoming less dependent on systems that leave us with little agency.

Episodes range from food, farming, land, and local production to economics, culture, technology, political philosophy, and the institutions that shape our lives. The common thread is a simple question: what can we actually build, improve, and influence from where we stand?

The Agrarian Librarian is about becoming more capable, more connected, and more deliberate about the lives and communities we build.
